Here's a detailed comparison of Visa and Mastercard's revenues based on their most recent SEC filings:

---

## 💳 Visa vs. Mastercard — Revenue Comparison

> **Note on Fiscal Years:** Visa's fiscal year ends **September 30**, while Mastercard's ends **December 31**. So their periods don't perfectly align on the calendar.

---

### Most Recent Fiscal Year Revenue

| Company | Fiscal Year End | Revenue | YoY Growth |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Visa (V)** | Sep 30, 2025 | **$40.00B** | +11.3% |
| **Mastercard (MA)** | Dec 31, 2025 | **$32.79B** | +16.4% |

- **Gap:** Visa leads Mastercard by **~$7.2 billion**, or roughly **22% more revenue**.

---

### 3-Year Revenue Trend (in billions USD)

| Fiscal Year | Visa | Mastercard |
|---|---|---|
| FY2023 | $32.65B | $25.10B |
| FY2024 | $35.93B | $28.17B |
| FY2025 | $40.00B | $32.79B |

---

### Key Takeaways

1. **Visa is the larger company by revenue** — consistently generating roughly 20–22% more than Mastercard across all three years shown.
2. **Mastercard is growing faster** — its most recent YoY growth was **+16.4%** vs. Visa's **+11.3%**, continuing a pattern where Mastercard has posted slightly higher growth rates.
3. **Both are on strong upward trajectories** — Visa grew revenues ~22% over two years; Mastercard grew ~31% over the same span, meaning the gap is slowly narrowing.
4. **Different fiscal calendars matter** — Mastercard's FY2025 includes Oct–Dec 2025, while Visa's FY2025 does not, so direct comparisons should be made with this in mind.

---

> ⚠️ *This is educational analysis based on SEC-reported figures, not investment advice. Past revenue growth does not guarantee future performance.*
